predecessors.name: French Fifth Republic
predecessors.text: French Chad, granted independence by France on 11 August 1960; Cliopatria carries this land in its French Fifth Republic row for 1958-1960

ledger.x: February 1978: Faya-Largeau falls and Libya-backed rebels take the north.
November 1981: Libyan forces leave Chad proper.
June 1983: Libya returns to the north.
11 September 1987: the OAU ceasefire ends the Toyota War.
May 1994: Libya leaves the Aouzou Strip.

wars.name: Chadian-Libyan conflict
wars.outcome: Chadian and French victory (infobox): the Toyota War of 1987 drove Libya from the BET Prefecture and ended in the 11 September 1987 ceasefire; Libya kept the Aouzou Strip until 1994.

wars.name: Aouzou Strip dispute
wars.outcome: The ICJ decided in February 1994 (16 to 1) for Chad's sovereignty; the Libyan withdrawal was completed by 10 May 1994 and the formal transfer took place on 30 May 1994 (these two dates from the Chadian-Libyan conflict page).

wars.name: Chadian Civil War
wars.outcome: 'In 1979 the rebel factions led by Hissene Habre took the capital.'

wars.name: Chad-Sudan war
wars.outcome: 'An agreement for the restoration of harmony between Chad and Sudan, signed 15 January 2010' ended a five-year war; the border reopened after seven years of closure.

certainty.note: The northern frontier with Libya is disputed until the 1994 judgment (Chad's claim rested on 1899 and 1955 instruments, Libya's on the unratified 1935 agreement); desert frontiers elsewhere are colonial lines the pages do not date.

The Libyan frontier is fixed by the ICJ judgment of 3 February 1994 and the withdrawal of May 1994; the Lake Chad shoreline stays soft; the pages opened give no instrument for the other frontiers (a judgment, not a source).
